articles.title: Signal Limits Mobile Screenshots to Combat AI Surveillance
articles.summary: Messaging platform Signal is restricting users from taking screenshots on both its Android and iOS applications. The move is described as a measure to confront what developers view as an existential threat posed by increasing AI surveillance.

articles.title: Actor Licenses Face to Startup in Microdrama Trend
articles.summary: An actor has licensed an AI version of his face to a microdrama startup, following a trend already popular in China. Industry experts are questioning the long-term consequences if this practice becomes widespread across Hollywood productions.

articles.title: Startup Sues Apple in India Over Feature
articles.summary: A U.S. startup is suing Apple in India, seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction that could impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports. The legal battle centers around a tap-to-share contacts feature developed by the startup.

articles.title: Spotify Founder Backs New Fusion Power Startup
articles.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is investing in Europa Fusion, a new fusion power startup created by an artificial intelligence researcher. The company aims to develop advanced clean energy solutions using innovative approaches inspired by recent technological advancements.

articles.title: AI and Humans Propose Solutions to Riemann Hypothesis
articles.summary: Mathematicians are reacting with surprise after an artificial intelligence system claimed a potential solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis. A competing solution proposed by a human researcher has also emerged, sparking widespread academic debate.

articles.title: Geothermal Energy Startups Target Data Center Power
articles.summary: New super-hot rock geothermal startups believe they can bypass traditional energy limits to deliver terawatts of electricity almost anywhere. The technology could provide a reliable power source to solve the massive energy demands of modern data centers.

articles.title: Amazon Adds Warning Labels Over New Delivery Rules
articles.summary: Amazon is placing warning labels on shipments in New York warning that a proposed Delivery Protection Act by the City Council could add up to $5 to customer orders. The controversial bill would effectively ban certain third-party delivery arrangements.

articles.title: UN Fails to Reach Agreement on Killer Robots
articles.summary: Diplomats meeting at the United Nations in Geneva concluded talks without establishing rules to regulate autonomous weapons, commonly known as killer robots. Representatives ultimately agreed only to start discussing future options following a largely unproductive week of negotiations.

articles.title: FBI and USDA Reportedly Target of Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Both the U.S. Department of Agriculture and the FBI were reportedly targeted in cyberattacks. The incident marks the second recent breach for the FBI, this time compromising the National Crime Information Center utilized by law enforcement agencies.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Could Reduce Global Farmland Demand
articles.summary: Widely used GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs could significantly decrease overall food demand. Researchers suggest the resulting shift in consumption might free up agricultural land an area larger than the country of Italy.

articles.title: Modern Genetics Refutes Claims of Racial Differences
articles.summary: Recent advancements in modern genetics continue to disprove outdated concepts of race realism. Scientific evidence demonstrates that genetic data does not support claims of innate racial differences in human intelligence.

articles.title: FCC Prevents California From Enforcing Phone Rules
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has preempted state regulations that previously required companies like AT&T to maintain traditional home phone service in California. The decision strips the state of its authority to enforce specific telecommunications mandates.

articles.title: Google Updates Search Page With AI Chat History
articles.summary: Google is redesigning its main search homepage to prominently feature artificial intelligence tools and chat history while removing the traditional search button. The update is designed to provide users with quicker access to conversational AI capabilities.

articles.title: Meta Reevaluates 2030 Net-Zero Goal Due to AI Growth
articles.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its corporate sustainability targets for 2030 as energy consumption and emissions from artificial intelligence data centers surge to record highs. The shift raises questions about whether other major tech companies will follow suit.

articles.title: Researcher Exposes Privacy Flaws in AI Supply Chain
articles.summary: By embedding trackable secret data markers into the artificial intelligence supply chain, a researcher demonstrated that confidential training data often fails to remain private, highlighting major security vulnerabilities in modern systems.

articles.title: Astronomers Observe Star Swallowing Neighbor
articles.summary: Scientists analyzing a recent unexpected burst of cosmic brightening discovered the phenomenon was caused by a star orbiting inside a larger neighbor before eventually being completely consumed and resulting in an explosion.

articles.title: Concerns Raised Over Prison Phone Jamming Tests
articles.summary: While prisons have received approval to use technology to jam contraband mobile phones, industry group CTIA warns that testing indicates the signal disruption can inadvertently interfere with nearby consumer phones up to two and a half miles away.

articles.title: Army Postpones Detonation of Hazardous Material
articles.summary: The U.S. Army has delayed plans to detonate a quantity of lead azide due to public fear and safety concerns. Environmental modeling predicted that the resulting plume of neurotoxic lead particles could travel as far as 100 miles away.
